::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="a13-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Who pays depends on the design</dt><dd>Per kWh the poorest group's burden rises 1.5 points, with a fixed charge 1.8 and by income 0.3, for the same $24M a year.</dd>
<dt>A transfer is not a cost</dt><dd>Moving from per kWh to a fixed charge shifts $1.34M a year between groups; the money moved adds up to zero.</dd>
<dt>Grouping changes the story</dt><dd>Below 80% of area median income the merged burden is 6.1%; the poorest group alone carries 14.9%.</dd>
<dt>Job-years are not jobs</dt><dd>7,200 job-years of building last two years; 1,840 permanent jobs lost add up to 36,800 job-years over 20 years.</dd>
<dt>Gross is not net</dt><dd>192 new permanent jobs gross, 154 net of displacement: a net change of −1,686 against the jobs lost.</dd>
<dt>Tax is a transfer</dt><dd>The county's revenue falls $30.0M a year; the owners pay that much less, so the region's resources do not change.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Real costs, transfers and real income-based designs</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **A real cost** uses something up: wires, equipment, labour, fuel. **A [transfer]{.lx-term term="transfer"}** moves money between people: taxes, rebates, a charge moved from one group to another.
- **Count each once.** Add real costs to judge a plan; read transfers to see who gains and who loses. Adding a transfer to a cost counts it twice.
- **Real designs.** California's regulator adopted a fixed charge in three income tiers for its large utilities ([income-based charge]{.lx-term term="income-based-charge"}; CPUC Decision 24-05-028, May 2024).

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Where real job and tax coefficients come from</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Input-output models.** NREL's JEDI models turn spending into jobs and count a construction job as one full-time year; they report gross jobs only.
- **Multipliers.** BEA's RIMS II sells regional multipliers for output, earnings and employment; new ones came out on 5 May 2026.
- **Baselines.** BLS's Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages counts jobs and wages by county and industry; DOE's USEER counts energy jobs by technology.
- **Taxes.** Rates, assessments and abatements are set by each state and county: read the local rules, not a national average.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The accounting layer, as a model you can reuse</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Take groups $g$ with $n_g$ households, income $y_g$, use $e_g$ (kWh) and home energy spending $s_g$. A yearly cost $C$ becomes a charge per household

$$c_g = \frac{C\,e_g}{\sum_h n_h e_h} \ \text{(per kWh)}, \qquad c_g = \frac{C}{\sum_h n_h} \ \text{(fixed)}, \qquad c_g = \frac{C\,y_g}{\sum_h n_h y_h} \ \text{(by income)}$$

- **Burden after:** $(s_g + c_g)/y_g$. Every design gives $\sum_g n_g c_g = C$, so the difference between two designs sums to zero: a transfer.
- **Jobs.** Net permanent jobs $= m\,(J_{\text{new}}(1 - d) - J_{\text{lost}})$, with multiplier $m$ and displacement $d$; building job-years $=$ spending in the county $\times$ job-years per \$M $\times\, m$.
- **Reuse.** The page's accounting is one small shared component, `whopays.js`, that the course's city sandbox and capstone can call with a plan's cost and its changes in use.
- **An energy model does not produce these outcomes by itself:** it gives costs, energy and MW; an accounting layer like this one turns them into who pays and who gains.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this lesson leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>How households and firms respond to prices, and how people move, retrain or start firms.</li>
<li>What the plan delivers to each group: cleaner air, lower bills from efficiency, reliability.</li>
<li>Who gets a say in the decision, as well as who pays.</li>
<li>Field surveys, interviews and causal studies of labour markets: the social-science methods behind real estimates.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
:::

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<p class="lx-lede">Practice, about 30 minutes: four myths, then six exercises with worked answers.</p>
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="a13-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="cheaper" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Moving a plan's cost from one group of households to another makes the plan cheaper.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Every design here recovers the same $24M a year; the money moved between groups adds up to zero, a transfer.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="fixed" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A fixed charge weighs most on low-income households.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. $237 a year is 1.8 points of burden for the poorest group and 0.2 for the top group.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="boom" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A two-year construction boom of 3,600 jobs replaces 1,840 permanent jobs.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. With this page's inputs, building gives 7,200 job-years; the lost jobs add up to 36,800 job-years over 20 years.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="tax" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “When a county loses a plant's property tax, the region loses that much wealth.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. The tax is a transfer: the county receives $30.0M a year less and the owners pay that much less; real for the county's budget, not for the region's resources.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card a13-practice">
<!-- a13-practice:start (written from the model by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Practice · about 30 minutes on your own</p><ol class="lx-fb-practice"><li><p><b>The per-kWh rate by hand.</b> Prairie City's households use 1,162,169,159 kWh a year. What rate recovers $24M?</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$24M ÷ 1,162,169,159 kWh = $0.0207, about 2.07¢ a kWh.</p></details></li><li><p><b>A fixed charge against income.</b> Split $24M equally over 101,410 households. How much does it add to the burden of a household earning $13,000?</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$237 a year each; 236.66 ÷ 13,000 = 1.82%, so +1.8 points.</p></details></li><li><p><b>The same share of income.</b> By income, what share of its income does every household pay?</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$24M ÷ total household income $8,428M = 0.285%; +0.3 points for every group.</p></details></li><li><p><b>Group, then read.</b> Households below 80% of area median income: how does their merged burden compare with the poorest group's, before the plan?</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Merged: total spending ÷ total income = 6.1%; the 0–30% group alone: 14.9%. The merged average hides the tail.</p></details></li><li><p><b>Job-years against jobs.</b> $1,500 per kW for 2,000 MW, 30% spent locally, 5.0 job-years per $M, multiplier 1.6. Compare with 1,840 permanent jobs lost over 20 years.</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$3,000M × 30% = $900M; × 5.0 × 1.6 = 7,200 job-years, against 1,840 × 20 = 36,800 job-years lost.</p></details></li><li><p><b>The county's budget.</b> Plant value $3,000M, new farms $3,000M with 50% taxable, rate 2.0%. What changes for the county, and for the region?</p><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$60M lost, $30M gained: −$30M a year for the county; for the region a transfer, owners pay less and the county receives less.</p></details></li></ol><p class="lx-hint">Screening estimate: your inputs and the stated assumptions, not a prediction. Prairie City is fictional; its numbers are illustrative. Ridge County and Prairieland are fictional; their numbers are illustrative.</p>
<!-- a13-practice:end -->
</div>
```
